summary: The Tribunes' Commonwealth: three states of red earth where the towns rose against a king in 4A 1719, now free among kings and wary of loans.

tribunes_charter.name: The Tribunes' Charter
tribunes_charter.desc: The charter was written in a single night by the leaders of the rising and has been amended once since. Every tribune swears to it on red earth, and every child can recite its first article.

red_banners.name: The Red Banners
red_banners.desc: The rising's banners hang in the tribunes' hall, faded from crimson to rust. Each year they are carried through the streets, and each year they are carried a little more proudly.

red_earth.name: Red Earth Farms
red_earth.desc: The red soil is poor in the dry months and rich after the rains, and its farmers have learned to ride both. A farm of red earth feeds more mouths than a farm of grey.

republic_stands.name: The Commonwealth Stands
republic_stands.desc: Kings waited for the commonwealth to fail, and it has not. Its towns are proud of that, and a little stubborn about it.

red_militia.name: The Militia of the Red Lands
red_militia.desc: Every household keeps a spear, a shield and a place in a militia company. They drill at the town gate on market days, between the cheese and the cloth.

day_of_the_red_banners.title: The Day of the Red Banners
day_of_the_red_banners.desc: The towns keep the day they set up the commonwealth, with banners in every window and a bonfire on every hill. The tribunes ask how the day should be kept this year.

an_example_to_the_east.title: An Example to the East
an_example_to_the_east.desc: Envoys from a neighbouring court ask how a commonwealth keeps its wells in the hands of its people. The tribunes look at one another, and then at the envoys' purses.

focuses.name: The Tribunes' Commonwealth
focuses.desc: In 4A 1719 the towns of the Red Lands rose against a king who had sold their wells to his creditors, and set up the rule of elected tribunes. Tribune Arcon Vel is its first magistrate.

focuses.name: The Tribunes' Charter
focuses.desc: The charter binds every tribune to the wells, the walls and the common storehouse. Kings call it the Red Charter, and say it will not last.

focuses.name: The Townsmen's Assembly
focuses.desc: Every householder of the three states may vote in the assembly, and tribunes are chosen from the benches by lot and by show of hands. The assembly is loud and slow.

focuses.name: The Free Charter
focuses.desc: The charter is read aloud at every crossroads, and every landholder swears to keep it. No one rules for longer than a year, and no one rules alone.

focuses.name: The First Tribune
focuses.desc: A single tribune is made first among the others, with a seal and a guard. The old men of the towns warn that this is how kings begin.

focuses.name: The Red Banners Endure
focuses.desc: The faded banners are hung in the new tribunes' hall, and the oath is sworn beneath them. Whatever else changes, the towns will remember what they are.

focuses.name: The Red Lands
focuses.desc: Red hills, red rivers and red clay roofs: the three states are as bright as a ripe pomegranate. The tribunes send surveyors to count every field and every well.

focuses.name: Red Earth Farms
focuses.desc: Farmers learn to sow when the rains come and plough when they leave, and each household stores seed against a bad year. Every field has its name carved on a stone.

focuses.name: Quarries of Red Stone
focuses.desc: Red sandstone is cut in the hills and floated to the towns on barges. The tribunes' hall is built of it, and so is half the commonwealth's pride.

focuses.name: The Dye Works
focuses.desc: Madder, ochre and a rare red clay are ground, boiled and set in vats beside the river. The cloth of Avalon is sold across the south in every shade of rust.

focuses.name: Salt of the Red Lands
focuses.desc: Salt-pans on the dry lakes yield grey crystals that are packed in clay jars and sold by the load. A dry summer is a good one.

focuses.name: The Red Road
focuses.desc: A road of packed red clay joins the three towns, ditched on both sides and lined with milestones. Wagons that once took a week now take three days.

focuses.name: Free Among Kings
focuses.desc: Kings around the Red Lands wait for the commonwealth to fail, and the tribunes know it. The council resolves to owe no one and to answer every letter.

focuses.name: Neighbours in Oreton
focuses.desc: Oreton lies across the southern hills, a small court with a long border and a longer memory. A pact of friendly neighbours is offered and accepted over a shared jar of wine.

focuses.name: The Bankers at the Door
focuses.desc: Postondoroth's agents arrive with a chest of silver and a pleasant offer. The tribunes know what the silver costs and what it buys, and take time to weigh both.

focuses.name: Owe No Prince
focuses.desc: The tribunes write the pledge on a bronze plate: no loan from a crown, no tribute to a throne. The commonwealth is poorer for it and freer by every year.

focuses.name: An Example to the East
focuses.desc: Envoys from the surrounding courts come to see how a commonwealth keeps its wells in the hands of its people. The tribunes show them the cisterns and the storehouse.

focuses.name: The Commonwealth Stands
focuses.desc: Five years pass, then ten, and the commonwealth is still free. Its towns keep the walls mended and the banners clean.

focuses.name: Townsmen's Levies
focuses.desc: Every householder is liable for a spear and a month's service, and every town has a muster-ground. The levies are poor soldiers and stubborn ones.

focuses.name: The Militia of the Red Lands
focuses.desc: The militia drills on market days at the town gate, in red caps and rough boots. A man who misses three drills pays a fine in grain.

focuses.name: Forts of the Commonwealth
focuses.desc: Low red-stone forts are raised at the river fords and the hill passes. They are plain and thick, and the militia can man them in an hour.

focuses.name: Pikes and Bows
focuses.desc: The militia drills with pikes and short bows, the arms of men who cannot afford a knight's horse. Bowmakers set up in the market squares.

focuses.name: The Commonwealth's Captains
focuses.desc: Captains are chosen by the militia companies and confirmed by the tribunes. They serve for a year and are obeyed for that year.
